{{Top}} {{Update|[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]}} {{Character |type=Galactic Empire |image=[[File:VerisHydan-WolvesAndADoor.png]] |name=Veris Hydan |homeworld=[[Ossus]]''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' |birth= |death=[[1 BBY]],{{RebelsDate|413}} [[Lothal]]{{Rebels|A World Between Worlds}} |species=[[Human]]{{Databank|veris-hydan|Veris Hydan}} |gender=[[Gender|Male]] |pronouns=new |height= |mass= |hair=[[Color|Gray]]{{Rebels|Wolves and a Door}} |feathers= |eyes=Blue |skin=Light |cyber= |families= |parents= |partners= |siblings= |children= |affiliation=*[[Galactic Empire]] **[[Ministry for Antiquity]]''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'' |masters= |apprentices= }} {{Quote|I would never consider myself an artist, but more a critic, perhaps.|Veris Hydan|}} '''Veris Hydan''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] who served the [[Galactic Empire|Galactic]] [[Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Palpatine]] as an [[Emperor's adviser|adviser]]. He also served as the [[minister]] of the [[Ministry for Antiquity]]. Although he was not [[Force-sensitive]], Hydan was a [[scholar]] of [[Jedi]] and [[Sith]] lore and history, as well as ancient and vanished cultures. He was also a [[Mortisologist]]. When the Empire discovered the [[Lothal Jedi Temple|Jedi Temple]] on the [[planet]] [[Lothal]], the minister was dispatched to oversee the [[Excavation of the Lothal Jedi Temple|excavation operations]] and to unlock the mysteries hidden beneath it, specifically an entrance to the [[World Between Worlds]]. During the excavation, Hydan encountered the disguised rebel infiltrators [[Sabine Wren]] and [[Ezra Bridger]], who had disguised themselves as [[scout trooper]]s. After Sabine was caught by Hydan's forces, Bridger managed to escape into the [[portal]] to the World Between Worlds. Then, Hydan attempted to use Wren to decipher the [[Painting of the Mortis gods|mural]] of the [[Force wielder|Mortis gods]], the gateway to the World Between Worlds. However, Sabine rejected his offer to decipher the mural and provided very little to Hydan, even after Hydan's [[death trooper]]s attacked Wren, she didn't provide anything to him. Shortly afterwards, the rebels [[Hera Syndulla]] and [[Garazeb Orrelios]], who were spying on the Minister and his troops, and also watching over the fellow infiltrators, invaded the excavation site and made the [[mobile command center]] in which Wren and Hydan were in shake and move until Wren could escape. Although Hydan needed more time to escape, he managed to exit the building. Shortly after they escaped, the young Bridger exited the World Between Worlds and the temple started to collapse. When the Rebels began their escape, Hydan admired the Mortis Gods' mural in his last moments. ==Biography== ===Excavating the Temple=== {{Quote|We have reached the roots of the Temple and found some fascinating work. The symbols and iconography are reminiscent of a report I discovered in the Jedi archives|Hydan to Emperor Palpatine|}} [[File:Hydan_reports_to_the_Emperor.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Hydan reports on the progress of the excavation to the Emperor.]] Veris Hydan was [[Reproduction|born]] on the [[planet]][[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] of [[Ossus]] and at some point he became a [[Minister]] and served the [[Galactic Empire]], he was a scholar in [[Jedi]] and [[Sith]] history and lore. He was also one of the Empire's leading [[Mortisologist]]s and scholars on ancient and vanished cultures.''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]'' The [[Ministry for Antiquity]] was founded under his control as a way of locating and collecting various artifacts important to [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]]. He served the Emperor, and was given a [[Veris Hydan's guard|personal guard]] of [[death trooper]]s. Following the discovery of the [[Lothal Jedi Temple]] in [[3 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of "[[Shroud of Darkness]]" to [[3 BBY]]. Hydan was dispatched to [[Lothal]] to [[Excavation of the Lothal Jedi Temple|excavate]] and to decipher the temple's mysteries. As the [[Mining Guild]] had already been operating on the planet,{{Rebels|Crawler Commandeers}} the Empire employed many of its personnel. The excavation site was heavily guarded by [[scout trooper]]s, [[stormtrooper]]s and death troopers. Hydan and the Emperor were very interested in the [[Portal|Gateway]], which supposedly led to the [[World Between Worlds]]. To avoid erasing any evidence to understanding the "Gateway," or any information that Palpatine could use, Minister Hydan issued orders that no Imperial personnel were allowed to touch any objects excavated from the temple. In [[1 BBY]], the Imperial excavation project attracted the attention of the [[Spectres]] rebel cell including the Jedi [[Ezra Bridger]], the [[Padawan]] of the late [[Jedi Knight]] [[Kanan Jarrus]]. When the rebels arrived at the temple, the Spectres divided, Syndulla and Orrelios used some [[binoculars]] to observe the excavation site while Bridger and Wren attacked a scout trooper displaying a hologram of [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo]]'s message to the rebels during the [[Battle of Atollon|siege of Atollon]]. While the troopers were confused by the hologram, Orrelios attacked them and obtained their uniforms, which he gave to the young rebels. [[File:Hydan-Explanation.png|thumb|right|300px|Hydan interrogates the disguised rebels]] Disguised as scout troopers, Bridger and Wren infiltrated the excavation site, when they reached the excavated artifacts, Bridger crouched and began to observe them with the Mandalorian. Shortly after the rebels began examining the art and artifacts, Minister Hydan stumbled upon the two examining art and ordered them to get away from it, shortly after, escorted by his death troopers, he began to examine the artifacts and art that was touched by the rebels. He then stated that he had already stated that no personnel, other than the Mining Guild, was to touch the excavated objects. And then added that the minimal loss of evidence could lose the possibility of understanding the gateway. Bridger then inquired the minister what was the gateway, however, he shortly interrupted himself and apologized for his behavior. After a death trooper of his escort informed the Minister that Coruscant, specifically, the Emperor wanted to contact him, the minister then told the commanding death trooper that the conduct of the scout troopers reflected poorly on him. Then, Minister Hydan departed with the rest of the escort and left the death trooper commander to deal with the two scout troopers. Immediately after the incident, the commander asked the troopers their numbers and clearance numbers. However, Bridger used a [[The Force|force mind trick]] on the commander which made the commander's desire to knowing the numbers and clearance numbers of the latter nonexistent. Inside the [[Mobile command center]], Minister Hydan informed the Emperor that the excavation had reached the roots of the temple and uncovered a [[painting of the Mortis gods]], which was reminiscent of art and iconography found at the former [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant]]. Hydan believed that the painting was the key to unlocking the "Gateway." The Emperor told Hydan that he sensed a great disturbance in [[the Force]] and opined that the death of Kanan had altered the fate of Lothal. Vowing to control the conduit between the living and the dead, the Emperor ordered Hydan to hasten his efforts. ===Interrogating Sabine=== {{Quote|I'm smarter than you.''"
"''I have informed the Emperor that your friend entered the temple. He was rather impressed with young Bridger. It must be so difficult for him without his master. Yes.''"
"''Kanan Jarrus, or Caleb Dume... Whichever|Sabine Wren and Veris Hydan|}} [[File:HydanAndMortisGodsPainting-SWRS04E13.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Hydan uncovers a picture of the Mortis gods]] Unknown to Hydan, his conversation was being tapped by the Spectres, whose droid [[C1-10P|Chopper]] had rerouted the Imperial transmission. Acting on this information, Bridger and Wren began to unlock the painting of the [[Force wielder|Mortis gods]], which was the "Gateway." Though Wren was taken away for questioning by a group of stormtroopers, Bridger managed to unlock the "Gateway" by touching the [[Daughter]]'s hand. Meanwhile, the stormtroopers brought Wren into Hydan's office for questioning. After identifying Wren as a rebel spy, Minister Hydan ordered that the camp be locked down because an intruder was on the loose. Minister Hydan, several troopers, and the captive Wren arrived at the "Gateway" but were unable to stop Bridger from entering the portal. A stormtrooper tried to follow but the portal sealed and he got himself hit with a wall. In response, Hydan had Wren brought into his mobile command center for questioning. Recognizing Wren as the talented [[Mandalorian]] rebel artist, Hydan attempted to flatter her while he drank some [[tea]]. When Hydan asked Wren how she and Bridger had entered the portal, the Mandalorian refused to cooperate. Hydan then mocked Bridger's master Kanan, also mocking his two names, Caleb Dume and Kanan Jarrus, prompting Wren to tell him that he was a pawn of the Emperor. Hydan countered that his power was a reflection of the Emperor's might. When Wren mocked the Emperor for failing to unlock the "Gateway," Hydan claimed that Bridger was not safe inside the World Between Worlds and that the Emperor would eventually find him. Hydan then told Wren that the "Gateway" was a pathway to time and that whoever controlled it controlled the universe. Continuing his interrogation, Hydan told Wren about the Mortis gods, a family of three powerful [[The Ones|beings]] known as the [[Father (Mortis)|Father]], Daughter, and the [[Son]]. When Hydan asked about the differences in their depiction on the Temple and Lothal mural, Wren feigned ignorance and unrespect towards him. Hydan then warned her not to mistake his "pleasant demeanor" for weakness and observed that the positions of the Loth–wolves, the Daughter's head, and the Father's hand had changed since Bridger's arrival. When Wren defiantly taunted him, Hydan ordered one of the death troopers to strike her across the head with his rifle butt. ===Last stand on Lothal=== {{Quote|What have they done? The knowledge...Everything will be lost! No!|Hydan's last words|}} [[File:Hydan-lost.png|thumb|right|250px|Hydan laments the loss of knowledge shortly before his death.]] After reasserting his authority by attacking Wren through one of his pawns, Hydan and Wren then discussed the painting of the Mortis gods. They concluded that the Daughter opened the portal while the Son closed it. In the meantime, Bridger had heard the voices of [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Yoda]], which he asked various answers to, but got no response. Shortly after, he found [[Ahsoka Tano]]{{Rebels|A World Between Worlds}} and [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] fighting in [[Malachor]]{{Rebels|Twilight of the Apprentice}}, when Tano was going to die at the hands of the Sith Lord, Bridger caught her shoulder and pulled back, causing her to leave the duel and survive it. After they greeted each other, and discussed the World Between Worlds and the possibility of saving Bridger{{'s}} master. Shortly after their meeting, Palpatine used [[Sith alchemy]] to unleash a [[Fiery energy]] attack on the two, however, they were able to stop the Emperor's attack. Tano promised Bridger that he would return with them, and Bridger departed while Tano used the Force to shield the young padawan and herself. After Bridger departed. Hera activated one of the thrusters beneath the mobile command center, causing the structure to rise and fall on its back. Wren managed to escape with her fellow Spectres and headed towards the painting. They were joined by Bridger, who had escaped the Emperor's clutches. Bridger convinced his fellow Spectres, including Wren, to help him seal the portal. [[File:Hydan-death.png|thumb|left|250px|Hydan falls towards his death]] Hydan arrived with several Imperial troops but the rebels managed to escape on a [[Mining Guild excavation driller]]. The sealing of the portal caused the Lothal Jedi Temple to collapse on itself. As the temple sunk into the ground in a blinding flash, Hydan lamented through a scream that the knowledge contained in the Temple would be lost. He then fell into a chasm, which killed him. ===Legacy=== The Ministry for Antiquity continued to function well after Hydan's death until it was dissolved in the aftermath of the [[Battle of Endor]]. Hydan's notability as a scholar for the ancient Jedi and Sith was known even well after his death. Some of his works were still in circulation as far as the aftermath of the [[Battle of Exegol]], a fact that was acknowledged by historian [[Beaumont Kin]], who in writing for the book ''[[The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'', expressed his regret at having to reference Hydan's work in their own writings. Kin also acknowledged the invaluable role that Hydan must have provided to Palpatine in being able to identify relevant ancient objects while discerning their functions. Kin further pointed out that many of the ancient sites that survived in the records of their time seemed to have been pillaged by the time Kin and his colleagues were able to get there. It was Kin's hypothesis that Hydan himself had likely undertaken at least some of these excavations. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|Remember? I'm smarter than you.''"
"''Lady Wren, I had hoped we could have a civil conversation about art, but I see the Mandalorian in you only understands one form of discourse.|Wren and Hydan on their meeting|}} [[File:HydanAndDeathTroopers-SWRS04E12.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Hydan and his death troopers]] Veris Hydan was a [[human]] [[Gender|man]] with light skin and blue eyes. He wore a dark headgear and a [[zeyd cloth|zeyd-cloth]] tunic in an [[ottdefa]]'s cut. Hydan was a scholar of Jedi and Sith history and lore. Due to his expertise in those topics, he was made in charge of the excavation of the Lothal Jedi Temple. Unlike his Sith master, he was not [[Force-sensitive]]. Hydan considered himself an art critic and used these skills to investigate the painting of the Mortis gods, which he discerned was a portal to the World Between Worlds. Hydan managed the excavation of the Lothal Jedi Temple with an iron grip and issued strict orders that no personnel were allowed to touch any of the artifacts, to avoid erasing evidence. Hydan was an astute man who quickly discerned that Sabine Wren was a rebel infiltrator. [[File:Hydan-discourse.png|thumb|left|250px|Hydan had a hatred for non-civil conversations]] He was also a philosophical man who preferred to use words and flattery rather than force when questioning Wren. However, Hydan was still prepared to use force against a defiant Wren and ordered a death trooper to strike her with his rifle butt. Hydan recognized that whoever controlled the World Between Worlds also controlled time and the fate of the universe. Hydan was a loyal servant of the Emperor and considered his own power to be a reflection of the Emperor's might. Hydan was distraught when the Spectres denied the Emperor access to the World Between Worlds and believed that the Emperor's fate was lost. ==Behind the scenes== Veris Hydan first appeared in "[[Wolves and a Door]]" and "[[A World Between Worlds]]," back-to-back episodes in the [[Star Wars Rebels Season Four|fourth season]] of the [[canon]] animated television show ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]''. The episodes aired in [[2018]], and Hydan was voiced by guest star [[Malcolm McDowell]]. At Dragon Con 2018, ''Rebels'' showrunner [[Dave Filoni]] revealed that Hydan was actually created by [[Henry Gilroy]] for the show's [[Star Wars Rebels Season Three|third season]], where he was supposed to have a bigger presence and be the mystical villain to the Jedi characters. Gilroy envisioned Hydan with an archaeological background who worked for the Emperor. His role would be that of scouring the galaxy for Jedi Temples, erasing them yet extracting secrets from them.{{WebCite|url=https://thewookieegunner.com/2018/09/08/star-wars-animation-panels-highlights-dragon-con/#more-17162|text=Highlights of the 'Star Wars' Animation Panels at Dragon Con 2018|date=2018-09-08|work=TWG|nobackup=1}} [[File:Vanee-GalacticFiles2018.png|thumb|right|200px|Vaneé, the character who was to fill Hydan's part in ''Rebels'' originally]] In earlier versions of the story for "Wolves and a Door," Hydan was intended to be [[Vaneé]], [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader's]] attendant from the [[2016]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|''Star Wars'' Anthology]] film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', but it was decided to make Hydan a new, separate character, although his design was still inspired by the one of the advisers who crowded around Vader and the Emperor.{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/wolves-and-a-door-trivia-gallery|text="Wolves and a Door" Trivia Gallery}} [[Pablo Hidalgo]] also stated that, according to what he remembered, Vaneé's name was created for ''Rebels''.{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|status/1729252329378271552|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=Vaneé was gonna be in REBELS, and I believe the name originated there, but as the REBELS story shifted and his fate became more clouded, he was renamed Hydan to avoid any possible conflicts. Navigating concurrent productions requires this. |archiveurl=https://archive.is/CQpmw}} For the episodes, Hydan's character model was created by [[Luke Harrington]].{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/wolves-and-a-door-behind-the-scenes-gallery|text="Wolves and a Door" Behind-the-Scenes Gallery}} {{C|Image 8}} In "Wolves and a Door" and "A World Between Worlds," Hydan was only identified by his surname. The name "Veris" was first used in the corresponding episode guides and [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]] entry posted on [[StarWars.com]] following the episodes' broadcast. The [[2019]] reference book ''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' established Ossus as the homeworld of Veris Hydan. The author [[Adam Bray]] wanted to make a meaningful [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] connection. He also noted the irony of an Imperial Advisor being born on the planet that once housed the [[Great Jedi Library]], a repository of all Jedi knowledge.{{Twitter|authoradambray|1316959074005716992|[[Adam Bray]]|quote=I love creating connections in Star Wars canon to meaningful Expanded Universe history. Thus in Ultimate Star Wars I designated the homeworld of Veris Hydan as Ossus. The Imperial archaeologist & advisor was born on a planet once housing an ancient Library of all Jedi knowledge.|archivedate=20210428153736}} ==Appearances== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of Veris Hydan}} *{{Rebels|Wolves and a Door}} {{1st}} *{{Rebels|A World Between Worlds}} ==Sources== *{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/a-world-between-worlds-episode-guide|text="A World Between Worlds" Episode Guide | Star Wars Rebels}} *{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/wolves-and-a-door-episode-guide|text="Wolves and a Door" Episode Guide | Star Wars Rebels}} {{1stID|Veris}} *''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' *''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' *''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]'' *''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'' *''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' *{{Databank|veris-hydan|Veris Hydan}} ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |de=Veris Hydan#kanon |es=Veris Hydan |fr=Veris Hydan |ka=ვერის ჰაიდენი }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Hydan, Veris}} [[Category:Archaeologists of the Galactic Empire]] [[Category:Humans]] [[Category:Imperial Advisors]] [[Category:Males]] [[Category:Scholars]]
